text: {"score":3,"justification":"Numbers match the card and the leaning of inconclusive is cautious and consistent with the hybrid_review output (undecided, too few documented 99215 claims). The rationale gives useful figures: 13.9% vs 2.9% expected, z_adj 10.87, 35% of 99215s on low-complexity patients, and 0 of 3 documented 99215s below billed. The next step to request more records is sensible. But the headline \"30/30 charts support billing\" overstates: only 3 of the 30 charts were 99215, and the summary itself says the records are too thin to judge, so the headline contradicts the body. \"Charts show no level mismatch\" is also too strong given the thin sample. The cited examples are two low-complexity claims, with no high-complexity contrast and no documented-supported examples. C0313134 is a COPD patient with 1 condition, a weak example. The rationale says \"Elevated in every group\" without explaining it, and the next steps don't name specific claims to request. The weak plain z of 1.69 versus adjusted 10.87 is left unexplained. The summary does not flag that 2 of the 3 documented 99215 claims (C0313741, C0313960) were low-complexity patients with high MDM, which is relevant to weighing the evidence.","problems":["Headline \"30/30 charts support billing\" is misleading: only 3 of the 30 charts were 99215 and the body says the sample is too thin","\"Charts show no level mismatch\" overstates what 3 documented 99215 claims can show","Large gap between plain z (1.69) and adjusted score (10.87) is not explained","Cited examples are only two low-complexity claims; one has a single condition and is weak; no documented claims cited, though two low-complexity 99215s (C0313741, C0313960) were documented as high MDM","Next steps are generic: no specific claim IDs or sample size to request","\"Elevated in every group\" is vague and not tied to the complexity table"]}
